newsitem.title: USA: Jurors chosen to hear Florida tobacco lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Jurors chosen to hear Florida tobacco lawsuit.

text.p: Six jurors were chosen Tuesday to hear a wrongful death lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, and lawyers said they expected opening statements to be made Wednesday.

Lawyers winnowed a 25-member jury pool to eight on Tuesday, the second day of jury selection in Raulerson vs. R.J. Reynolds, a case in which the sister of a smoker who died of lung cancer has accused the tobacco company of peddling a deadly product.
Of the eight, six will serve as jurors. But Judge Bernard Nachman asked reporters covering the case not to reveal details that would identify the six selected for the jury.
The judge will call 10 people from a second jury pool early Wednesday. From that group of 10 and the pair remaining from the group of eight, two will be selected as alternate jurors for the trial.

Included in the group of eight chosen Tuesday were a woman who claimed to be allergic to cigarette smoke, a woman who began smoking at age 15, a man who quit smoking and a woman who is an occasional smoker.
Among the prospective jurors who were dismissed Tuesday was a woman who said she felt "very strongly against R.J. Reynolds" because she was owed $1,400 by the company for modeling work.

Lawyers asked the prospective jurors questions about their personal lives, their feelings about cigarettes and tobacco companies, addiction and their beliefs about personal and corporate responsibility.

The lawsuit alleges that Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, deceived the public about the dangers of cigarettes. Reynolds' attorneys have contended that the late Jean Connor, who died of cancer in 1995 at age 49, and whose sister Dana Raulerson brought the case, made an informed decision to smoke.
